performance-oracle-no-trace.name: performance-oracle-no-trace
command:
import argparse,importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('d3_reference_timing','tools/oracle/d3_turbo/trace.py')
m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);spec.loader.exec_module(m)
class QuietTrace:
    def __init__(self,*args):pass
    def emit(self,*args,**kwargs):pass
    def record(self,*args,**kwargs):pass
m.Trace=QuietTrace
m.main(argparse.Namespace(model=Path('models/d3-turbo'),request=Path('target/d3-turbo/one.json'),out=Path('target/d3-turbo/coverage/performance-oracle-no-trace.jsonl'),threads=8,official=False,device='cpu',gguf=None,activation_quantization=False,vision_only=False))

limitations: End-to-end diagnostic timings include model loading; F32 Oracle includes trace payload I/O.
A failed strict Vulkan attempt is not a GPU inference timing.
Official BF16 and the native F32 execution use different activation precision.
Earlier runs with concurrent conversion, different thread counts or administrative pauses are not throughput comparisons.
The isolated official GPU attempt was terminated during loading at the container memory bound, before inference. It is neither an observed OOM exception nor a GPU inference timing.
CPU and GPU setup failures are archived separately; the corrected CPU BF16 retry passed and the corrected cuda:0 GPU retry did not reach inference.
The no-trace F32 reference runs the same graph with a QuietTrace sink; its diagnostic end-to-end time includes Python startup and model loading.
CPU reference environment additionally uses project-local accelerate 1.13.0 and psutil 7.2.2; GPU Torch reuses the preinstalled host ROCm environment.
